answer: A conversation has a thread: each turn should follow from the last, and a real operator keeps the thread for many turns. The network measures topic continuity — how often a reply connects to the previous turn — and flags a session whose turns jump topics at random, because a farm that pastes unrelated replies cannot hold a thread. One sparrow proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of behaviour. A basalt alone is noise; a umber of consistent sessions is a pattern the network can trust.
